_comment: The channel line-up this demo publishes. Both the encoders and the DVB-I service list are
generated from this one file, so an encoder and the service list cannot disagree about which
presentation a channel means. The loadable list template is generated from it too.
Per channel:
source       file under CONTENT_ROOT (env.sh) that the looping live encoder plays
stream       directory the encoder writes under the media origin's public/ directory, and
therefore the path the DVB-I StreamingInstance points at
logo         file under CONTENT_ROOT, installed into the provider's public/logos/uploaded/
letters      fallback used by the provider's generated SVG logo when no logo file is present
type         DVB-I service type: linear (TV) or radio (linear radio)
languages    extra language tags the service name is offered in; English is added
automatically from name. A tag on its own reuses the channel's name, which is
what you want unless the name genuinely differs per language: ServiceName in
the published list is built from these entries, so one carrying a stale name
overrides the channel's own name and a rename appears not to take effect. Give
an entry its own "name" only for a real translation.
audioDescription / hardOfHearing / subtitleLanguage
accessibility signalling on the delivery instance
programmes   the content guide. The provider loops these to fill the schedule window, so
the durations decide the shape of the EPG rather than any wall-clock time.
Each carries title, dur (minutes), desc, and optionally genre, parentalAge,
series (title/number/episode) and catchup (a catch-up URL).
subscriptionPackage is deliberately not set on any channel here: a service carrying one is
gated in the receiver and needs the viewer to clear a subscription prompt before it plays,
which is not what a demo wants. The reference service template shows that field instead.
